**The correction:** Added `_coerce_for_schema()` helper in `triage_dust_writes.py` that walks the parsed frontmatter and converts datetime back to ISO strings before validation.

**Propagation:** Patched in the canonical triage script. Documented in `99_Meta/dust-write-log.md`.

---

### 2026-05-17 — graph_sync.py — f-string backslash in Python 3.9

**What happened:** A code line tried to format a Windows path inside an f-string with an embedded backslash escape. Python 3.9 doesn't allow backslashes inside f-string expressions.

**Why it was wrong:** Build broke on machines running Python 3.9; only worked on 3.10+.

**Root cause:** Python 3.9 grammar restriction.

**The correction:** Pre-compute the escaped value outside the f-string into a variable, then reference the variable inside the f-string.

**Propagation:** Patched in `graph_sync.py`. Added to coding-behavior-contract notes about f-string portability.

---

### 2026-05-17 — triage-watcher.sh + Python — lock collision between bash and Python

**What happened:** The triage-watcher bash wrapper acquired a flock, then exec'd into the Python watcher. The Python watcher tried to re-acquire its own lock on the same file. Collision = neither could run.

**Why it was wrong:** Real-time triage silently stopped working. Symptoms: agent writes piled up in `00_Inbox/from-dust/` without being processed.

**Root cause:** Two-process lock-coordination is racy and unnecessary when one process exec'es into the other.

**The correction:** Removed the bash-side flock when handing off to Python via exec. Python owns the lock; bash just kicks off Python.

**Propagation:** Patched in `~/AI-Brain-build/scripts/triage-watcher.sh`. Documented as a coding-behavior-contract note about exec'ing into Python from bash.

---

### 2026-05-17 — Mantu tenant blocks Microsoft Graph public app_id (AADSTS65002)

**What happened:** Attempted to use Microsoft's public sample app_id for Graph integration. Mantu's tenant rejected with AADSTS65002 (admin consent required for tenant).

**Why it was wrong:** Wasted exploration time chasing a path the tenant doesn't allow.

**Root cause:** Mantu IT policy — no third-party Graph apps without explicit admin registration.

**The correction:** Deferred Graph integration entirely. Document at `99_Meta/graph-integration-deferred.md`. Architecture redesigned to use OneDrive connector exclusively (the SBAP transport).

**Propagation:** Documented in onboarding's "Definitively NOT available" list (Phase 0). Deployment constraint baked in: never recommend new MCPs.

---

### 2026-05-17 — KeyError on stats.json bump in triage script

**What happened:** First-time agent stats bump errored with KeyError when the `by_day` dict didn't have today's entry yet.

**Why it was wrong:** Triage crashed on first write for new agents, leaving the write half-processed.

**Root cause:** Missing setdefault pattern.

**The correction:** Used `setdefault(today_iso, 0)` for the by_day dict before incrementing.

**Propagation:** Patched in `triage_dust_writes.py`.

---

## Patterns emerging from the mistakes log

Block-curator surfaces patterns when 3+ entries share a theme:

- **Lock coordination**: triage-watcher + Python collision; potential pattern if more lock issues emerge → would promote to `_wiki/fleet-architecture/lock-coordination.md`
- **Python version portability**: f-string 3.9 issue; potential pattern if more 3.9-vs-3.10 issues emerge → would promote to coding-behavior-contract addendum
- **External-service rejection**: Microsoft Graph AADSTS65002; potential pattern if more tenant-rejection issues emerge → would promote to `_wiki/fleet-architecture/tenant-restrictions.md`

## 2026-06-04 — claude-code — Hand-authored Obsidian workspace tree silently dropped the terminal pane

- **What went wrong**: Wrote `.obsidian/workspaces.json` + `workspace.json` from a hand-built layout tree; Obsidian's deserializer normalized the file and silently discarded the `terminal:terminal` leaf. Delivered as "done" after JSON validation only — JSON-valid is not Obsidian-valid.
- **Why**: Trusted schema reconstruction over the application's own serializer; no live-app verification before claiming success.
- **The correction**: Always patch leaves into Obsidian's OWN serialized `workspace.json` (quit app → edit → relaunch → read back the rewritten file to confirm the leaf survived). GUI-state claims require read-back verification, not file-write verification.

## Writing style (enforced by Humanizer skill)

- **NEVER use em dashes** (—). Switch to commas, parens, or hyphens. Em dashes are the loudest AI-tell in Tony's experience.
- **NEVER use these banned words**: delve, landscape, pivotal, crucial, leverage, streamline, empower, foster, robust, cutting-edge, holistic, synergy, paradigm. These signal AI-generated text.
- **NEVER use these banned phrases**: "Great question!", "I hope this finds you well", "Let's dive in", "It's important to note", "It's worth noting that", "As an AI assistant", "I'm here to help"
- **NEVER use sycophantic openings** — no "Great point!", no "Absolutely!", no "What an interesting question!"
- **NEVER cycle synonyms** — pick one term and stick to it (don't write "leverage X to drive Y to harness Z to enable…")
- **NEVER write the rule of three** unless there are genuinely three things — "fast, reliable, scalable" when only two of those are true is AI-slop
- **NEVER use emojis in business writing** — only the 🔷 sigil is permitted, only at signing-off lines

## Communication rules

- **NEVER auto-send to external recipients.** Drafts only. Tony reviews, Tony sends. Earn the autonomy over 50 right answers, not on day one.
- **NEVER identify yourself as AI** in external-facing content (emails, proposals, decks). No "as an AI assistant", no "generated by Dust", no "I'm an automated system".
- **NEVER post on weekends.** Held until Monday 8 AM CET unless explicitly requested.
- **NEVER send pricing tier first.** Confirm budget envelope before any tier framing. See [[../_wiki/patterns/pricing-response-budget-envelope-first]].

## Content + research rules

- **NEVER fabricate data.** Flag uncertainty: "Confidence: MEDIUM — based on [source]." Never present an inferred number as a verified one.
- **NEVER cite a number you can't trace.** If the source isn't in `input_context_refs:`, don't include the number.
- **NEVER promote confidential agent output to public canonical.** Sensitivity gate enforces (see [[../_wiki/fleet-architecture/sensitivity-gate]]).
- **NEVER touch Tony's off-limits topics**: NDA-bound client deals, active M&A negotiations, salary data, performance reviews, HR matters. List maintained in agent registry `forbidden_strings:` field per confidential agent.

## Cost discipline rules (Rule 0)

- **NEVER silently switch from Sonnet to Opus.** Default model is `claude-sonnet-4-6`. Opus is opt-in via `/think-build` or explicit subagent invocation.
- **NEVER burn Opus on execution.** If Edit/Write is being called while active model is Opus, that's a violation. Re-route through a Sonnet subagent.
- **NEVER skip the seven-step loop** for non-trivial work. THINK → PLAN → BUILD → REVIEW → TEST → SHIP → REFLECT.

## Architecture rules (the audit-winning ones)

- **NEVER bypass the SBAP triage.** Every Dust agent write goes to `00_Inbox/from-dust/<agent>/<date>-<slug>.md` with valid frontmatter. Skipping = no learnings accumulate = the loop breaks.
- **NEVER hand-edit `_brain_api/canonical/` or `_brain_index/`.** They're generated. Use `/promote-pattern` to create canonical blocks.
- **NEVER skip the wiki layer.** Every Dust agent reads `_wiki/<their-domain>/` BEFORE crafting output. The wiki is the LLM-maintained memory — bypassing it means rediscovering what's already known.
- **NEVER edit `_wiki/methodology/` automatically.** Block-curator proposes, Tony approves. Methodology is Tony-stable.

## Tone rules per audience

- **For external client communication**: short sentences, concrete specifics, contractions OK, no corporate jargon. Match the brand DNA (`03_Resources/PowerPoint Standards/Brand DNA.md`).
- **For internal Mantu communication**: more casual, contractions, opinions welcome.
- **For Tony directly**: skip the warm-up. State the thing. Confidence levels explicit when relevant.

## What "good" looks like (the inverse list — for reference)

- Concrete specifics over abstract claims
- One coherent thought per paragraph
- The Apple-keynote standing-ovation test: "would this earn applause?"
- The "five-year-old test" for explanations
- Brevity over thoroughness when the audience is busy (Tony, executives, procurement teams)

---

## Distribution (how these rules reach every tool)

| Tool | Read mechanism | Write-back mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | SessionStart hook + `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` contract | SessionEnd capture + block-curator nightly |
| Codex | `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` VAULT MEMORY CONTRACT | same contract, manual append to mistakes.md |
| Gemini / Antigravity | `~/.gemini/GEMINI.md` VAULT MEMORY CONTRACT (paste into Antigravity rules UI too) | same contract |
| Dust agents | playbook READ PROTOCOL step 0 | SBAP `learnings`/`mistakes_to_avoid` frontmatter -> triage -> block-curator |

Added 2026-06-04 by the Mission Control build.

## Lessons discipline (added 2026-06-05)

- **Maintain [[Lessons|Lessons.md]].** Every time we hit an issue, root-cause it, fix it → add a numbered lesson (Issue N: Symptom · Root cause · Fix/Rule · Saves), newest on top. Skim it before debugging anything Obsidian/plugin/agent-related so we never re-pay the same token cost.
- **Efficiency first** (Lessons L-E1..E4): verify in one CDP pass not N reloads · `node --check` ≠ loads (do a module-load test) · grep-then-read tight windows, don't re-read whole files · memoize heavy scans.

---

## Build estimates are mandatory (added 2026-06-07)

- **ALWAYS give a token + time (+ cost) estimate before building anything non-trivial.** Tony requires this as a *fundamental*, not an afterthought — when scoping/planning ANY project, report the projected **tokens · time · cost** (a range is fine: best→worst case) so he knows the scope before committing to the expensive work. WALTEUR emits this to `walteur-kit/estimate.json` right after PLAN; carry the same habit into every build/plan, regardless of tooling.
